chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, and from Ibn Muskhan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
We found in the book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'Regarding the partridge, if the person in ihram kills it, and it is a young bird that has weaned from milk and eats from trees.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.حَمَلٌ: A young bird (specifically one that has weaned from milk)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for killing a partridge while in ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the authority of the *Kitab Ali* (Book of Ali), a foundational juristic text attributed to Imam Ali (AS), in establishing specific details of *kaffarah* (expiation) for hunting errors during Hajj or Umrah. By specifying a young bird that has weaned from milk and feeds on vegetation, the hadith demonstrates the precise biological criteria used in Shia fiqh to determine the value of the compensation, reflecting the meticulous legal methodology of the Imams.
